title: Attribution ledger edge -- causal relation between two pieces of work
description: v3 (2026-08-25, Merlini/Pavlo -- the commons stops at attribution, sizing is out). v2 hardcoded a `counts_toward_vertice_split` derivation rule -- a single company's compensation logic living inside a format explicitly meant to belong to no one. Merlini named the concrete asymmetry: his own real contributions (verifying ReceiptOS's artifacts, work landing in invinoveritas) had no way to ever 'count' under a scheme that only special-cased Vertice. Pavlo's framing, adopted here: 'commons attribution record -> owner-specific compensation policy.' This file now records ONLY what happened, causally -- a foundation discovery/audit/method applied to (or enabling, or depended on by) another surface, and who independently verified that causal link. Whether any given edge counts toward ANY owner's compensation is that owner's own private policy, read from this record -- never a field this schema defines. See README.md's 'Reading edges for your own compensation policy' section for how an owner (Vertice, invinoveritas, or anyone else) builds that policy on top of this data without it living in the commons.

edge_type.description: Closed enum, owner-neutral. 'dependency': a surface uses a foundation artifact/tool without any deliberate, verified act of applying a specific discovery to it. 'verified_application': a specific foundation discovery/audit/spec-correction/method was DELIBERATELY applied to a named commercial_product surface, and that application itself was independently verified. 'enabling_provenance': the reverse direction -- a commercial/product surface enabled foundation work to exist. All three are recorded identically as attribution -- this schema does not rank them by whether any of them 'counts' toward anyone's compensation; that judgment belongs to whichever surface owner is reading the record for their own policy.

source_entry.description: The `entry_id` (schema.json) this edge originates from -- a real, independently-verified ledger entry, not a free-form string. If the thing being applied/depended-on/enabling doesn't have a ledger entry yet, write that entry first; an edge cannot point at something unrecorded.

target.description: The `entry_id` (schema.json) of what the source was applied to, depends on, or enabled. Same rule as source_entry -- must be a real ledger entry's id, resolvable to that entry's own `surface` field (classification + identifier + owner_id when commercial). This is the concrete fix for Merlini's dinamic.eth/boiler-kit/ai.verticecriativo.pt case: recording that enabling_provenance edge requires a real ledger entry for the enabling surface to exist first (a `build` entry describing what it was and when), not a bare description inline on the edge.

edge_verified_by.description: REQUIRED and non-empty when edge_type is 'verified_application' (enforced below, not just documented); optional/absent otherwise. Verifies the CAUSAL LINK ITSELF -- that the application actually happened and actually caused the target -- a different, additional verification from whichever verified_by already exists on the source entry's own claim.

timestamp.description: When the causal relation is recorded (not necessarily when either endpoint's own entry was made). An actual event timestamp, not a round/approximate one.

source_contribution_ref.description: The exact foundation contribution being applied -- restates source_entry's own entry_id for readability, or points at the specific sub-part of it (a file, a function) that was actually applied. Required for verified_application.

target_surface_ref.description: The exact surface/feature/release/claim the contribution was applied to -- a commit, release tag, or product-facing reference, not a repo name alone. Required for verified_application. Owner-neutral: this is whichever commercial_product (or commons, or external) surface target resolves to, not specifically a Vertice one.

causal_link_verification.description: How the causal link itself (not just the source claim) was independently confirmed -- what the edge_verified_by parties actually checked. Required for verified_application.
